more.title: Detroit Lions Longtime Chair Emeritus Martha Firestone Ford Dies
more.desc: DETROIT - Martha Firestone Ford, longtime Detroit Lions owner and chair emeritus, died at 101, the team announced Tuesday. Ford owned the NFL franchise for more than six decades, helping guide the organization from 1963 through its transition to the next generation of family leadership. Ford took over sole control of the franchise in 2014 following the death of her husband, William Clay Ford, who originally purchased the team in November 1963. She served as principal owner until 2020, when she transitioned into an emeritus role and transferred day-to-day leadership of the franchise to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp. Alongside Hamp, her other three children—Martha Ford Morse, William Clay Ford Jr. and Elizabeth Ford Kontulis—each serve as team vice chairs.

more.desc: Six people, including two children, have been found dead after a plane crashed off the coast of Mississippi on Tuesday, according to the Coast Guard. Divers found their bodies in the fuselage of the aircraft after the Cessna 210 went down in the Gulf of Mexico between Pascagoula, Mississippi, and Horn Island, which is part of the Gulf Islands National Seashore, according to officials. There were four adults and two boys, ages 8 and 10, on board, said Coast Guard spokesperson Juan Ros.
